name: dup
text: Copy the top item.
examples: : sq dup * ;
: fact ( n -- n! ) dup 1 > if dup 1- recurse * then ;
: colours 8 1 do i dup 3 lshift or rgb! 400 ms loop 0 rgb! ;

name: drop
text: Remove the top item.
examples: pin-ss low $9F 0 spi-xfer drop 0 0 spi-xfer . pin-ss high   \ e.g. a flash's ID
: mirror begin btn@ led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;
begin 0 led-toggle 1 led-toggle 300 ms key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: swap
text: Exchange the top two items.
examples: : run-time ( -- ms ) ms@ pg-start begin pg-status 4 and until ms@ swap - ;
wait-btn ms@ swap - 0 led!
: level ( -- n ) 0 adc@ 820 / 1 swap lshift 1- ;

name: over
text: Copy the second item to the top.

name: nip
text: Remove the second item.

name: tuck
text: Copy the top item below the second.

name: rot
text: Rotate the third item to the top.

name: -rot
text: Rotate the top item to third place.

name: 2dup
text: Copy the top two items.

name: 2drop
text: Remove the top two items.
examples: : blink ( n -- ) begin dup led-toggle 250 ms key? until key 2drop ;

name: ?dup
text: Copy the top item only if it is not zero.

name: depth
text: Number of items on the data stack, before depth itself pushes.

name: .s
text: Show the stack without changing it: <3> 1 2 3, with the depth and the top on the right.

name: >r
text: Move the top item to the return stack.
examples: >r fn !  fover f- r@ s>f f/ h f! x0 f!

name: r>
text: Move the top of the return stack back.
examples: r> drop h f@ f* 3e f/ ;

name: r@
text: Copy the top of the return stack.
examples: >r fn !  fover f- r@ s>f f/ h f! x0 f!
0 f(i) r@ f(i) f+
r@ 1 do i f(i) i weight f* f+ loop

text: Sum.
examples: table 2 cells + ? 4  ok
create ftab 1e f, 2e f, 4e f,  ftab 2 floats + f@ f. 4.  ok
: five [ 2 3 + ] literal ;  ok

text: Difference n1 − n2.
examples: : run-time ( -- ms ) ms@ pg-start begin pg-status 4 and until ms@ swap - ;
wait-btn ms@ swap - 0 led!

text: Product, low 32 bits; one instruction (hardware multiplier, 3 clocks).
examples: : sq dup * ;
: fact ( n -- n! ) dup 1 > if dup 1- recurse * then ;
: table 3 1 do 3 1 do j i * . loop loop ;

text: Quotient, rounded toward zero: -7 2 / gives −3.
examples: : level ( -- n ) 0 adc@ 820 / 1 swap lshift 1- ;

name: mod
text: Remainder, with the sign of n1: -7 2 mod gives −1.

name: /mod
text: Remainder and quotient (symmetric division).

name: u/mod
text: Unsigned division: -7 2 u/mod gives 1 2147483644.
n1 × n2 / n3 with a 64-bit intermediate product, so the product may exceed 32 bits: 100000 100000 1000 */ gives 10000000. Rounds toward zero.

name: um*
text: Full 64-bit unsigned product as two cells, the high cell on top: -1 -1 um* gives 1 −2 (4294967294).

name: um/mod
text: Divide a 64-bit unsigned number by u. The quotient must fit in 32 bits (high cell < u).

name: (um/mod)
text: The divide instruction itself: the quotient; the remainder stays in the divider for (urem).

name: (urem)
text: The remainder of the last (um/mod). Use it directly after it.

name: s>d
text: Extend a number to a double number with the same value: -5 s>d gives −5 −1.

name: dnegate
text: Change the sign of a double number.
Add one.
examples: : sq sq 1+ ;   \ the inner sq is the old one
: delay sw@ 1+ 100 * ms ;
: bump 1000 0 do 0 lock shared @ 1+ shared ! 0 unlock loop ;   \ on both cores

text: Subtract one.
examples: : fact ( n -- n! ) dup 1 > if dup 1- recurse * then ;
: level ( -- n ) 0 adc@ 820 / 1 swap lshift 1- ;

text: Double.
Arithmetic shift right; keeps the sign (-8 2/ gives −4).

name: negate
text: Change the sign.

name: min
text: Smaller of two signed numbers.

name: max
text: Larger of two signed numbers.

name: and
text: Bitwise AND.
examples: 5 led!   \ LD0 and LD2 on
1 led-on   \ LD1 on as well: LD0, LD1 and LD2 are lit
0 led-off   \ LD0 off: LD1 and LD2 stay

name: or
text: Bitwise OR.
examples: : colours 8 1 do i dup 3 lshift or rgb! 400 ms loop 0 rgb! ;

name: xor
text: Bitwise exclusive OR.

name: invert
text: Invert all bits. Also turns a true flag into false and back.

name: lshift
text: Shift left by u bits; u ≥ 32 gives 0.
examples: : runner begin 4 0 do 1 i lshift led! delay loop key? until key drop 0 led! ;
: colours 8 1 do i dup 3 lshift or rgb! 400 ms loop 0 rgb! ;
: level ( -- n ) 0 adc@ 820 / 1 swap lshift 1- ;

name: rshift
text: Logical shift right by u bits (fills with 0); u ≥ 32 gives 0.

name: arshift
text: Arithmetic shift right by u bits (fills with the sign bit): -8 2 arshift gives −2, while -8 2 rshift gives 1073741822.
Equal.
examples: : find3 10 0 do i 3 = if ." found" unloop exit then loop ." none" ;

text: Not equal.
n1 less than n2, signed.
n1 greater than n2, signed.
examples: : fact ( n -- n! ) dup 1 > if dup 1- recurse * then ;

name: u<
text: Less than, unsigned: -1 1 u< is false.

name: u>
text: Greater than, unsigned.
x is zero; also a logical NOT.
examples: : wait-free begin btn@ 0= until ;
: count-press 1 presses +! presses @ led! begin btn0? 0= until ;
: watch2 begin 2 pin@ 0= 1 and led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;

text: x is not zero.
n is negative.
n is positive.

name: within
text: lo ≤ n < hi; works for signed and unsigned ranges.
Fetch the cell at a (bits 0 and 1 of a ignored).
examples: $100020 @ 255 and .   \ read IO0..IO7 at once
: count-press 1 presses +! presses @ led! begin btn0? 0= until ;
: f(i) ( i -- ) ( F: -- y ) x(i) fn @ execute ;

text: Store x at a.
examples: variable x  5 x !  3 x +!  x ? 8  ok
255 $100028 !   \ IO0..IO7 as outputs
170 $100024 !   \ IO1, IO3, IO5, IO7 high, the others low

name: c@
text: Fetch the byte at a.

name: c!
text: Store the low byte of c at a.
Add n to the cell at a.
examples: variable x  5 x !  3 x +!  x ? 8  ok
: bump 1 count +! ;
: count-press 1 presses +! presses @ led! begin btn0? 0= until ;

text: Print the cell at a, like @ ..
examples: variable x  5 x !  3 x +!  x ? 8  ok
table 2 cells + ? 4  ok
." BTN0 pressed " presses ? ." times" cr ;

name: cells
text: Size of n cells in bytes.
examples: table 2 cells + ? 4  ok

name: cell+
text: Address of the next cell.

name: aligned
text: Round a up to a multiple of 4.

name: cmove
text: Copy u bytes from a1 to a2, lowest address first.

name: fill
text: Store the byte c in u bytes from a: buf 8 32 fill fills 8 bytes with spaces.

name: here
text: Address of the next free byte.

name: allot
text: Reserve n bytes at here (a negative n gives memory back).
examples: create buffer 20 allot

name: align
text: Round here up to a multiple of 4.
Align, store x at here, advance by one cell.
examples: create table 1 , 2 , 4 , 8 ,

name: c,
text: Store a byte at here, advance by one byte.
examples: create msg 104 c, 105 c,   \ "hi"

name: key
text: Wait for a character from the terminal.
examples: : mirror begin btn@ led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;
: alternate ( -- )   \ LD0 and LD1 take turns; any key stops
begin 0 led-toggle 1 led-toggle 300 ms key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: key?
text: True if a character is waiting (does not take it).
examples: : mirror begin btn@ led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;
begin 0 led-toggle 1 led-toggle 300 ms key? until key drop 0 led! ;
: runner begin 4 0 do 1 i lshift led! delay loop key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: emit
text: Send a character (waits while the send FIFO is full).
examples: 65 0 uart-emit  1 uart-key emit A  ok
msg 2 1 uart-type  0 uart-key emit 0 uart-key emit hi ok

name: cr
text: New line (sends CR and LF).
examples: : hello ." Hello, Arty!" cr ;
." wait for the LEDs..." cr
." reaction time " . ." ms" cr

name: space
text: Send one space.

name: spaces
text: Send n spaces (nothing for n ≤ 0).

name: zeros
text: Send n zeros, the character 0 (nothing for n ≤ 0); used by f..

name: type
text: Send u characters starting at a.
Print a signed number in the current base, then a space.
examples: led@ .   \ prints 6
btn@ .   \ hold BTN1 while pressing Enter: prints 2
13 pin@ . -1  ok

name: u.
text: Print an unsigned number, then a space: -1 u. gives 4294967295.
Compile only: print text when the definition runs.
examples: : hello ." Hello, Arty!" cr ;
: find3 10 0 do i 3 = if ." found" unloop exit then loop ." none" ;
: shout ." loud" ; immediate

text: Print text immediately, in a definition or at the terminal.

name: base
text: Variable holding the base for number input and output (2..36).

name: hex
text: Set the base to 16.

name: decimal
text: Set the base to 10.

name: led!
text: Set LD0..LD3 from bits 0..3 of n (1 = on).
examples: 5 led!   \ LD0 and LD2 on
: count16 16 0 do i led! 250 ms loop 0 led! ;
: mirror begin btn@ led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: led@
text: Read back the LED state.
examples: led@ .   \ prints 6

name: led-on
text: Switch LED n (0..3, LD0..LD3) on; the other LEDs stay as they are.
examples: 1 led-on   \ LD1 on as well: LD0, LD1 and LD2 are lit
0 led! 0 led-on

name: led-off
text: Switch LED n (0..3) off; the other LEDs stay as they are.
examples: 0 led-off   \ LD0 off: LD1 and LD2 stay

name: led-toggle
text: Change LED n (0..3): on becomes off, off becomes on.
examples: : blink3 10 0 do 3 led-toggle 200 ms loop ;   \ LD3 blinks 5 times, the others stay
begin 0 led-toggle 1 led-toggle 300 ms key? until key drop 0 led! ;
: blink ( n -- ) begin dup led-toggle 250 ms key? until key 2drop ;

name: led-mask
text: The bit of LED n in led! (1 for LD0 … 8 for LD3); "bad led" for n outside 0..3.

name: btn@
text: Buttons: bit 0 = BTN0 … bit 3 = BTN3, 1 = pressed. Debounced (sampled every 10 ms).
examples: btn@ .   \ hold BTN1 while pressing Enter: prints 2
: mirror begin btn@ led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;
: wait-btn begin btn@ until ;

name: sw@
text: Switches: bit 0 = SW0, bit 1 = SW1, 1 = on.
examples: : delay sw@ 1+ 100 * ms ;

name: rgb!
text: RGB LEDs: bits 0/1/2 = LD4 red/green/blue, bits 3/4/5 = LD5 red/green/blue.
examples: 9 rgb!   \ LD4 red, LD5 red
: colours 8 1 do i dup 3 lshift or rgb! 400 ms loop 0 rgb! ;

name: rgb@
text: Read back the RGB LED state.

name: ms
text: Wait n milliseconds (0..2147483647).
examples: : blink3 10 0 do 3 led-toggle 200 ms loop ;   \ LD3 blinks 5 times, the others stay
2 1 pwm-hz  100 1 pwm-duty  12 1 pwm-pin   \ IO12: 2 Hz, 50 ms pulses
250 2 pwm-duty  20 ms  0 mv@ . 880  ok

name: ms@
text: Millisecond counter, 32 bits; wraps every 2^32 ms (about 49.7 days).
examples: : run-time ( -- ms ) ms@ pg-start begin pg-status 4 and until ms@ swap - ;
2000 ms 15 led! ms@
wait-btn ms@ swap - 0 led!

name: us@
text: Microsecond counter, 32 bits; wraps every 2^32 µs (about 71.6 minutes).

name: output
text: Make the pin an output.
examples: 13 output  13 high   \ IO13 to 3.3 V
pin-ss output pin-ss high   \ the chip select, idle high
14 output  14 high  10 ms  0 mv@ .

name: input
text: Make the pin an input again.
examples: 13 low  13 input   \ back to an input
2 pin@ . -1  ok   \ an open input with pull-up reads high
14 low  10 ms  0 mv@ .  14 input

name: high
text: Set the pin's output latch to 1 (3.3 V when it is an output).
examples: 13 output  13 high   \ IO13 to 3.3 V
2 pin@ . -1  ok   \ an open input with pull-up reads high
1000 0 pwm-hz  250 0 pwm-duty  13 0 pwm-pin   \ IO13: 1 kHz, 25 % high

name: low
text: Set the output latch to 0.
examples: 13 low  13 input   \ back to an input
170 $100024 !   \ IO1, IO3, IO5, IO7 high, the others low
0 1 us pg-wait   \ 0: wait for BTN0, then 1 us low

name: toggle
text: Invert the output latch.
examples: : blink13 13 output begin 13 toggle 250 ms key? until key drop 13 low ;

name: pin!
text: high if f is true, otherwise low.

name: pin@
text: Read the level at the pin: true = high. Also works on outputs, where it reads back the driven level.
examples: 13 pin@ . -1  ok
2 pin@ . -1  ok   \ an open input with pull-up reads high
: watch2 begin 2 pin@ 0= 1 and led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: pin
text: Bit mask and port address of pin n; "bad pin" for numbers that are not shield pins.

name: bset
text: Set the mask bits in the cell at a (a general helper).

name: bclr
text: Clear the mask bits in the cell at a.

name: adc@
text: Raw result of channel 0..8: 0..4095 for 0 to full scale. "bad channel" for other numbers.
examples: : level ( -- n ) 0 adc@ 820 / 1 swap lshift 1- ;

name: mv@
text: The channel's voltage in millivolts at the shield pins.
examples: 0 mv@ . 5  ok   \ A0 open
250 2 pwm-duty  20 ms  0 mv@ . 880  ok
750 2 pwm-duty  20 ms  0 mv@ . 2413  ok

name: volts@
text: The channel's voltage in volts, as a float on the float stack (section 5.15). "bad channel" for numbers above 8.
examples: : avg-volts ( ch -- ) ( F: -- v ) 0e 100 0 do dup volts@ f+ loop drop 100e f/ ;

name: temp@
text: Chip temperature in tenths of a degree Celsius: 452 means 45.2 °C.

name: ftemp@
text: Chip temperature in degrees Celsius, as a float.
examples: ftemp@ f. 44.66434  ok

name: .temp
text: Print the chip temperature, for example 45.2 C.
examples: .temp 44.7 C  ok
supplies .temp
: thermo begin .temp cr 1000 ms key? until key drop ;

name: supply@
text: A supply voltage in millivolts, from XADC register reg (table below).
examples: 1 supply@ . 2 supply@ . 15 supply@ . 1018 1801 1489  ok
: supplies 1 supply@ . 2 supply@ . 6 supply@ . 13 supply@ . 14 supply@ . ;

name: xadc@
text: Raw 12-bit result of XADC status register reg (0..31).

name: vaux
text: Table of 9 bytes: the XADC auxiliary input of each channel (used by adc@).

name: pwm-pin
text: Route channel ch to the pin and start it. The pin becomes an output driven by the channel; "bad pin" for numbers that are not shield pins, "pin taken" for a pin another channel or peripheral owns (section 5.16).
examples: 1000 0 pwm-hz  250 0 pwm-duty  13 0 pwm-pin   \ IO13: 1 kHz, 25 % high
2 1 pwm-hz  100 1 pwm-duty  12 1 pwm-pin   \ IO12: 2 Hz, 50 ms pulses
100 2 pwm-khz  14 2 pwm-pin

name: pwm-off
text: Stop the channel and free its pin. The pin returns to its own latch and direction (an input after start-up).
examples: 0 pwm-off  1 pwm-off
2 pwm-off

name: pwm-hz
text: Frequency in Hz, 1..25000000.
examples: 1000 0 pwm-hz  250 0 pwm-duty  13 0 pwm-pin   \ IO13: 1 kHz, 25 % high
2 1 pwm-hz  100 1 pwm-duty  12 1 pwm-pin   \ IO12: 2 Hz, 50 ms pulses

name: pwm-khz
text: Frequency in kHz, 1..25000.
examples: 100 2 pwm-khz  14 2 pwm-pin

name: pwm-duty
text: Duty cycle in ‰ (tenths of a percent), 0..1000: 0 is always low, 1000 always high; values outside are clamped.
examples: 1000 0 pwm-hz  250 0 pwm-duty  13 0 pwm-pin   \ IO13: 1 kHz, 25 % high
500 0 pwm-duty   \ now 50 %
2 1 pwm-hz  100 1 pwm-duty  12 1 pwm-pin   \ IO12: 2 Hz, 50 ms pulses

name: pwm-clocks
text: The period directly, in 50 MHz clocks (20 ns), as a double number: low cell, then high cell, read like a duration (d>ticks, section 5.14). At least 2: 100000 0 0 pwm-clocks gives 500 Hz.

name: pwm
text: Register address of channel ch; "bad channel" for ch above 3.

name: ud/u
text: Unsigned 64-bit double divided by an unsigned single, giving a double quotient.

name: ns
text: u nanoseconds in ticks, rounded down to 5 ns: 100 ns = 20 ticks.
examples: 1 500 ns pg-step   \ 0: clock high
0 500 ns 0 999 pg-loop   \ 1: clock low; steps 0-1 play 999 times
3 500 ns pg-step   \ 2: clock and marker high

name: us
text: u microseconds: u × 200 ticks; u up to 21474836, larger gives "too long".
examples: 0 1 us pg-wait   \ 0: wait for BTN0, then 1 us low
0 2 us 0 pg-jump   \ 3: 2 us low, then wait again
0 1 0 pg-wait  $100 2 us pg-step  0 1 0 0 pg-jump  pg-start

name: msec
text: u milliseconds: u × 200,000 ticks; u up to 21474, larger gives "too long". Not ms: that word waits (section 5.10).
examples: pg-stop 0 pg-at  1 1000 msec pg-step  0 pg-end  run-time .   \ 1000
: counts 16 0 do i 250 msec pg-step loop ;
counts  15 pg-at  15 250 msec 0 pg-jump  pg-start

name: d>ticks
text: The ticks of a duration ( lo hi ): lo when hi is 0, otherwise lo + hi × 65536, the 16-bit style; "too long" when lo or hi is above 65535 then. The step and PWM words use it; us and msec refuse 2^32 ticks and more themselves ((dur)), so their doubles never get the 16-bit reading.

name: pg-at
text: The step the next step word stores, 0..4095.
examples: pg-stop  3 pg-enable  0 pg-idle  0 pg-at
pg-stop  3 pg-enable  0 pg-idle  48 1 pg-trigger  0 pg-at
pg-stop 0 pg-at  1 1000 msec pg-step  0 pg-end  run-time .   \ 1000

name: pg-step
text: Store a step: the levels (channel n = bit n) for d ticks, then the next step.
examples: 1 500 ns pg-step   \ 0: clock high
3 500 ns pg-step   \ 2: clock and marker high
3 500 ns pg-step   \ 1: clock and frame high

name: pg-loop
text: Store the last step of a repeat: after it, go back to step *target* until the steps *target*..this one have run *count* times in all; 0 = forever.
examples: 0 500 ns 0 999 pg-loop   \ 1: clock low; steps 0-1 play 999 times
2 500 ns 1 8 pg-loop   \ 2: clock low; steps 1-2 play 8 times

name: pg-jump
text: Store a step that continues at step *target* after it.
examples: 0 500 ns 0 pg-jump   \ 3: low; back to step 0, forever
0 2 us 0 pg-jump   \ 3: 2 us low, then wait again
counts  15 pg-at  15 250 msec 0 pg-jump  pg-start

name: pg-wait
text: Store a wait step: it shows its levels, waits for the trigger, then holds them for d ticks.
examples: 0 1 us pg-wait   \ 0: wait for BTN0, then 1 us low
0 1 0 pg-wait  $100 2 us pg-step  0 1 0 0 pg-jump  pg-start

name: pg-end
text: Store the end: the generator stops with these levels on the pins.
examples: pg-stop 0 pg-at  1 1000 msec pg-step  0 pg-end  run-time .   \ 1000

name: pg-start
text: Play from step 0 (also while playing: start again).
examples: pg-start
: run-time ( -- ms ) ms@ pg-start begin pg-status 4 and until ms@ swap - ;
counts  15 pg-at  15 250 msec 0 pg-jump  pg-start

name: pg-stop
text: Stop; the enabled channels go to their idle levels.
examples: pg-stop  3 pg-enable  0 pg-idle  0 pg-at
pg-stop  3 pg-enable  0 pg-idle  48 1 pg-trigger  0 pg-at
pg-stop 0 pg-at  1 1000 msec pg-step  0 pg-end  run-time .   \ 1000

name: pg-trig
text: The software trigger: a waiting step goes on.

name: pg-enable
text: Which channels the generator drives (bit n = channel n).
examples: pg-stop  3 pg-enable  0 pg-idle  0 pg-at
pg-stop  3 pg-enable  0 pg-idle  48 1 pg-trigger  0 pg-at
pg-stop  $F pg-enable  0 pg-at

name: pg-idle
text: The levels while stopped.
examples: pg-stop  3 pg-enable  0 pg-idle  0 pg-at
pg-stop  3 pg-enable  0 pg-idle  48 1 pg-trigger  0 pg-at

name: pg-trigger
text: What wait steps wait for. Source: a shield pin 0..41, 48..51 for BTN0..BTN3, 63 for the software trigger only. Edge: 1 rising, 2 falling, 3 both. pg-trig works with any source.
examples: pg-stop  3 pg-enable  0 pg-idle  48 1 pg-trigger  0 pg-at
pg-stop  $100 pg-enable  49 1 pg-trigger  0 pg-at

name: pg-status
text: The status bits, below.
examples: : run-time ( -- ms ) ms@ pg-start begin pg-status 4 and until ms@ swap - ;
pg-status .   \ 3: playing and waiting

name: pg-pc
text: The step playing now.

name: pg-out@
text: The levels on the channels now.

name: pg-sync
text: Wait until the generator has taken the last command or setting (about 0.1 µs). The words above that command or set it do this themselves.

name: fdup
text: Copy the top float.
examples: : gauss ( F: x -- y ) fdup f* fnegate fexp ;

name: fdrop
text: Remove the top float.

name: fswap
text: Exchange the top two floats.
examples: : scale ( -- ) 8 0 do 300 261.63e i s>f 12e f/ 2e fswap f** f* beep loop ;

name: fover
text: Copy the second float to the top.
examples: >r fn !  fover f- r@ s>f f/ h f! x0 f!

name: frot
text: Rotate the third float to the top.

name: fnip
text: Remove the second float.

name: fdepth
text: Number of floats on the float stack.

name: f.s
text: Show the float stack without changing it, like .s: <3> 1. 2.5 3..

name: f+
text: Sum.
examples: : x(i) ( i -- ) ( F: -- x ) s>f h f@ f* x0 f@ f+ ;
0 f(i) r@ f(i) f+
r@ 1 do i f(i) i weight f* f+ loop

name: f-
text: Difference r1 − r2.
examples: >r fn !  fover f- r@ s>f f/ h f! x0 f!

name: f*
text: Product.
examples: 9.81e fconstant g  g 2e f* f. 19.62  ok
: scale ( -- ) 8 0 do 300 261.63e i s>f 12e f/ 2e fswap f** f* beep loop ;
: deg ( F: degrees -- radians ) pi f* 180e f/ ;

name: f/
text: Quotient r1 / r2.
examples: 1e 0e f/ f. Inf  ok
: scale ( -- ) 8 0 do 300 261.63e i s>f 12e f/ 2e fswap f** f* beep loop ;

name: fsqrt
text: Square root; NaN for a negative r.
examples: : rt2 [ 2e fsqrt ] fliteral ;  rt2 f. 1.414214  ok
2e fsqrt fs. 1.414214E0  ok

name: fnegate
text: Change the sign.
examples: : gauss ( F: x -- y ) fdup f* fnegate fexp ;

name: fabs
text: Absolute value.

name: fmin
text: The smaller of the two.

name: fmax
text: The larger of the two.

name: ftrunc
text: Round toward zero to a whole number: -2.7e ftrunc gives −2.

name: floor
text: Round toward minus infinity: -2.5e floor gives −3.

name: fround
text: Round to the nearest whole number, halves to the even one: 2.5e fround gives 2, 3.5e fround 4.

name: f<
text: r1 less than r2.

name: f=
text: r1 equal to r2. fdup f= is false only for a NaN.

name: f>
text: r1 greater than r2.

name: f0<
text: r is negative.

name: f0=
text: r is zero.

name: f0>
text: r is positive.

name: s>f
text: Integer to float; exact up to 2^24 (16777216), rounded above.
examples: : scale ( -- ) 8 0 do 300 261.63e i s>f 12e f/ 2e fswap f** f* beep loop ;
: x(i) ( i -- ) ( F: -- x ) s>f h f@ f* x0 f@ f+ ;
>r fn !  fover f- r@ s>f f/ h f! x0 f!

name: f>s
text: Float to integer, toward zero: -3.99e f>s gives −3. Values beyond the integer range give −2147483648 or 2147483647; NaN gives 0.

name: u>f
text: Unsigned integer to float: -1 u>f gives 4.294967E9.

name: f>u
text: Float to unsigned integer, toward zero, for 0 ≤ r < 2^32; a negative r gives 0.

name: d>f
text: Double number (64 bits, section 5.3) to float.

name: f>d
text: Float to double number, toward zero, for |r| < 2^63: 1e15 f>d gives −1543503872 232830.

name: f>bits
text: The float's 32 bits, unchanged: 1e f>bits hex u. gives 3F800000.

name: bits>f
text: A float from its 32 bits: $40490FDB bits>f f. gives 3.141593.

name: >float
text: Convert the string a u, written like a float literal (above). On success the float goes to the float stack and f is true; otherwise f is false and the float stack is unchanged. An empty string gives false.

name: represent
text: Write the significant digits of r, rounded to u digits (at most 9), to the buffer at a, without sign or point. n is the decimal exponent, so that r = 0.ddd × 10^n; f1 is true if r is negative; f2 is false if r is a NaN or infinite.

name: f@
text: Fetch the float at a.
examples: fvariable speed  2.5e speed f!  speed f@ f. 2.5  ok
create ftab 1e f, 2e f, 4e f,  ftab 2 floats + f@ f. 4.  ok
: x(i) ( i -- ) ( F: -- x ) s>f h f@ f* x0 f@ f+ ;

name: f!
text: Store r at a.
examples: fvariable speed  2.5e speed f!  speed f@ f. 2.5  ok
>r fn !  fover f- r@ s>f f/ h f! x0 f!

name: sf@
text: The same as f@ and f!.

name: sf!
text: The same as f@ and f!.

name: f,
text: Align, store r at here, advance by one cell.
examples: create ftab 1e f, 2e f, 4e f,  ftab 2 floats + f@ f. 4.  ok

name: floats
text: Size of n floats in bytes.
examples: create ftab 1e f, 2e f, 4e f,  ftab 2 floats + f@ f. 4.  ok

name: sfloats
text: Size of n floats in bytes.

name: float+
text: Address of the next float.

name: sfloat+
text: Address of the next float.

name: faligned
text: Like aligned.

name: sfaligned
text: Like aligned.

name: falign
text: Like align.

name: sfalign
text: Like align.

name: fvariable
text: Create a float variable, initially 0. name then pushes its address.
examples: fvariable speed  2.5e speed f!  speed f@ f. 2.5  ok
variable fn  fvariable x0  fvariable h

name: fconstant
text: Create a float constant. name then pushes r on the float stack.
examples: 9.81e fconstant g  g 2e f* f. 19.62  ok

name: fliteral
text: Compile r as a float (immediate), like literal.
examples: : rt2 [ 2e fsqrt ] fliteral ;  rt2 f. 1.414214  ok

name: f.
text: Print r with precision significant digits, then a space. Fixed notation for 10^-7 ≤ |r| < 10^9, with trailing zeros removed and always a decimal point: 3.75, 0.3333333, 2.; otherwise scientific notation, also without trailing zeros: 1.E10, 3.4E38.
examples: ftemp@ f. 44.66434  ok
fvariable speed  2.5e speed f!  speed f@ f. 2.5  ok

name: fs.
text: Print r in scientific notation, always with precision digits: 3.333333E-1.
examples: 2e fsqrt fs. 1.414214E0  ok

name: fe.
text: Print r in engineering notation: the exponent is a multiple of 3, with 1 to 3 digits before the point: 12.34500E3.

name: precision
text: The number of significant digits the three words print: 1..9, 7 after start-up.

name: set-precision
text: Set precision; numbers outside 1..9 are taken as 1 or 9.
examples: 9 set-precision 0.1e f. 0.100000001  ok
7 set-precision 0.1e f. 0.1  ok

name: pi
text: The float nearest π, 3.141593.
examples: : deg ( F: degrees -- radians ) pi f* 180e f/ ;
1e fatan 180e f* pi f/ f.   \ prints 45.
0e pi ' fsin 100 simpson f.   \ prints 2.

name: fsin
text: Sine.
examples: 30e deg fsin f.   \ prints 0.5
0e pi ' fsin 100 simpson f.   \ prints 2.

name: fcos
text: Cosine.

name: fsincos
text: Sine and cosine, the cosine on top; faster than both separately.

name: ftan
text: Tangent.

name: fasin

name: facos
text: Arc cosine, 0..π; NaN for |x| > 1.

name: fatan
text: Arc tangent, −π/2..π/2.
examples: 1e fatan 180e f* pi f/ f.   \ prints 45.

name: fatan2
text: The angle of the point (x, y), −π..π: -1e -1e fatan2 f. gives −2.356194.

name: fexp
text: e^x; infinity above 88.72, 0 below −87.34.
examples: : gauss ( F: x -- y ) fdup f* fnegate fexp ;

name: fln
text: Natural logarithm; −Inf for 0, NaN for a negative x.

name: flog
text: Logarithm to base 10.

name: flnp1
text: ln(1 + x), accurate also for a tiny x: 1e-5 flnp1 fs. gives 9.999950E-6.

name: fexpm1
text: e^x − 1, accurate also for a tiny x: 1e-5 fexpm1 fs. gives 1.000005E-5.

name: f**
text: r1 to the power r2, computed as e^(r2 × ln r1): 2e 10e f gives 1024. A negative r1 needs a whole-number r2 (otherwise NaN); 0 to the power 0 is 1.
examples: : scale ( -- ) 8 0 do 300 261.63e i s>f 12e f/ 2e fswap f** f* beep loop ;

name: fsinh
text: Hyperbolic sine.

name: fcosh
text: Hyperbolic cosine.

name: ftanh
text: Hyperbolic tangent.

name: uart-open
text: Open UART u at the baud rate, sending on pin tx and receiving on pin rx: 115200 1 0 0 uart-open (TX on IO1, RX on IO0).
examples: 115200 26 27 0 uart-open  115200 28 29 1 uart-open   \ wires IO26-IO29, IO28-IO27

name: uart-close
text: Close it and free its pins.

name: uart-emit
text: Send a byte; waits while the send FIFO is full.
examples: 65 0 uart-emit  1 uart-key emit A  ok

name: uart-type
text: Send a string.
examples: msg 2 1 uart-type  0 uart-key emit 0 uart-key emit hi ok

name: uart-key?

name: uart-key

examples: 65 0 uart-emit  1 uart-key emit A  ok
msg 2 1 uart-type  0 uart-key emit 0 uart-key emit hi ok

name: uart-status
text: Bit 2: everything sent; bit 3: a received byte was lost because the FIFO was full; bit 4: a byte had no stop bit (wrong baud rate?). Reading clears bits 3 and 4.

name: spi-open
text: Open SPI master s on these pins; mode 0, 8 bits, 1 MHz until changed.
examples: pin-sck pin-mosi pin-miso 0 spi-open  1000000 0 spi-hz

name: spi-close
text: Close it and free its pins.

name: spi-hz
text: The SCK frequency: 25 MHz / an integer, at most 12.5 MHz (rounded down to the next possible one).
examples: pin-sck pin-mosi pin-miso 0 spi-open  1000000 0 spi-hz

name: spi-mode
text: Mode 0..3 (bit 1 CPOL: SCK idles high; bit 0 CPHA: data taken at the second edge).

name: spi-bits

name: spi-lsb
text: True: least significant bit first.

name: spi-xfer
text: One transfer: sends out, returns what came back.
examples: pin-ss low $9F 0 spi-xfer drop 0 0 spi-xfer . pin-ss high   \ e.g. a flash's ID

name: spi-write
text: Send n bytes from a (the answers are dropped).

name: spi-read
text: Receive n bytes into a (sending zeros).

name: i2c-open
text: Open the I2C master on SCL and SDA: 100000 i2c-open. First it frees the bus: 9 clocks on SCL and a stop, in case a slave was left in the middle of a read and still holds SDA (about 0.2 ms).
examples: 100000 i2c-open  i2c-scan

name: i2c-open-pins
text: The same on other pins.

name: i2c-close
text: Close it and free its pins.

name: i2c@
text: Read register reg of the device at addr: start, address+W, reg, repeated start, address+R, one byte, stop. "no ack" if the device does not answer.
examples: 0 $68 i2c@ .   \ its seconds register

name: i2c!
text: Write b into register reg of the device at addr.

name: i2c-scan
text: Print the address (in hex) of every device that answers, from $08 to $77.
examples: 100000 i2c-open  i2c-scan

name: i2c-probe
text: True if a device answers at addr.

name: i2c-addr
text: Start (or repeated start) and the address byte, rw 1 = read; true if acknowledged.

name: i2c-start
text: A start condition.

name: i2c-stop
text: A stop condition.

name: i2c-write
text: Send a byte; true if the device acknowledged it.

name: i2c-read
text: Receive a byte, then acknowledge it (true: more bytes follow) or not (false: the last one).

name: dds-hz
text: The frequency, a float: 1000000e dds-hz. Can change while it runs.
examples: 32768e dds-hz 13 dds-pin   \ a 32.768 kHz clock on IO13
1e6 dds-hz   \ now 1 MHz

name: dds-pin
text: Start it on the pin (or move it to another one).
examples: 32768e dds-hz 13 dds-pin   \ a 32.768 kHz clock on IO13

name: dds-off
text: Stop it and free the pin.
examples: dds-off

name: tone
text: Play the frequency: 440e tone. Can change while it plays.
examples: 50 volume sine wave  440e tone  1000 ms  tone-off

name: tone-off
text: Stop (the volume ramps down in 2 ms).
examples: 50 volume sine wave  440e tone  1000 ms  tone-off

name: wave

examples: 50 volume sine wave  440e tone  1000 ms  tone-off

name: sine

examples: 50 volume sine wave  440e tone  1000 ms  tone-off

name: square

name: triangle
text: The waveforms for wave: 0, 1, 2 and 3.

name: sawtooth
text: The waveforms for wave: 0, 1, 2 and 3.

name: volume
text: 0..100, 50 after start-up.
examples: 50 volume sine wave  440e tone  1000 ms  tone-off

name: beep
text: A tone for ms milliseconds: 200 880e beep.
examples: : scale ( -- ) 8 0 do 300 261.63e i s>f 12e f/ 2e fswap f** f* beep loop ;

text: Start a new definition called name and switch to compiling.
examples: : hello ." Hello, Arty!" cr ;

text: End the definition, make it findable, switch back to interpreting.
examples: : hello ." Hello, Arty!" cr ;
: blink3 10 0 do 3 led-toggle 200 ms loop ;   \ LD3 blinks 5 times, the others stay
: run-time ( -- ms ) ms@ pg-start begin pg-status 4 and until ms@ swap - ;

name: variable

name: constant

examples: 10 constant ten

name: create
text: Create a word that pushes the address of the data space following it; reserve that space with allot, , or c,.
examples: create table 1 , 2 , 4 , 8 ,
create ftab 1e f, 2e f, 4e f,  ftab 2 floats + f@ f. 4.  ok

name: immediate
text: Make the newest word immediate: it runs during compilation instead of being compiled.
examples: : shout ." loud" ; immediate

name: if
text: Run the code if f is true.
examples: : fact ( n -- n! ) dup 1 > if dup 1- recurse * then ;
: find3 10 0 do i 3 = if ." found" unloop exit then loop ." none" ;
begin btn0? if count-press then key? until key drop

name: then
text: Run the code if f is true.
examples: 0 1 us pg-wait   \ 0: wait for BTN0, then 1 us low
0 2 us 0 pg-jump   \ 3: 2 us low, then wait again
: fact ( n -- n! ) dup 1 > if dup 1- recurse * then ;

name: else
text: Choose between two branches.
examples: : weight ( i -- ) ( F: -- w ) 1 and if 4e else 2e then ;

name: begin
text: Repeat until f is true (runs at least once).
examples: : run-time ( -- ms ) ms@ pg-start begin pg-status 4 and until ms@ swap - ;
: mirror begin btn@ led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;
begin 0 led-toggle 1 led-toggle 300 ms key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: until
text: Repeat until f is true (runs at least once).
examples: : run-time ( -- ms ) ms@ pg-start begin pg-status 4 and until ms@ swap - ;
: mirror begin btn@ led! key? until key drop 0 led! ;
begin 0 led-toggle 1 led-toggle 300 ms key? until key drop 0 led! ;

name: while
text: Repeat while f is true, test in the middle.
examples: btn@ .   \ hold BTN1 while pressing Enter: prints 2
: quiet shout ;  loud ok   \ shout ran while quiet was compiled

name: repeat
text: Repeat while f is true, test in the middle.

name: again
text: Repeat forever (leave with exit, or Ctrl-R from the terminal).
examples: 0 2 us 0 pg-jump   \ 3: 2 us low, then wait again
: worker begin receive dup * send again ;   \ core 1

name: do
text: Counted loop: the index runs from start to limit − 1.
examples: : blink3 10 0 do 3 led-toggle 200 ms loop ;   \ LD3 blinks 5 times, the others stay
: scale ( -- ) 8 0 do 300 261.63e i s>f 12e f/ 2e fswap f** f* beep loop ;
: evens 10 0 do i . 2 +loop ;

name: loop
text: Counted loop: the index runs from start to limit − 1.
examples: : blink3 10 0 do 3 led-toggle 200 ms loop ;   \ LD3 blinks 5 times, the others stay
: scale ( -- ) 8 0 do 300 261.63e i s>f 12e f/ 2e fswap f** f* beep loop ;
: table 3 1 do 3 1 do j i * . loop loop ;

name: +loop
text: Like loop, but adds n to the index; ends when the index is ≥ limit. Counts upward only.
examples: : evens 10 0 do i . 2 +loop ;

name: exit
text: Return from the current word immediately.
examples: : find3 10 0 do i 3 = if ." found" unloop exit then loop ." none" ;

name: recurse
text: Call the word being defined.
examples: : fact ( n -- n! ) dup 1 > if dup 1- recurse * then ;

name: i
text: Index of the innermost loop.
examples: : scale ( -- ) 8 0 do 300 261.63e i s>f 12e f/ 2e fswap f** f* beep loop ;
: evens 10 0 do i . 2 +loop ;
: table 3 1 do 3 1 do j i * . loop loop ;

name: j

name: unloop

examples: : find3 10 0 do i 3 = if ." found" unloop exit then loop ." none" ;

text: Execution token of name; 0 if not found (standard Forth signals an error).

text: Compile only: compile name's xt as a literal.

text: Switch to interpreting inside a definition (immediate).

text: Switch back to compiling.

text: Ignore the rest of the line.

text: The registers of UART u ($100200 + 16 * u); "bad uart" for other numbers than 0 and 1.

name: spi
text: The registers of SPI master s ($100220 + 32 * s); "bad spi" for other numbers than 0 and 1.

name: (owner)
text: The pin's owner register ($100300 + 4 * pin, section 5.16, *Pin owners*).

name: (mine)
text: "pin taken" if the other core owns the pin.

name: (free)
text: "pin taken" unless the pin is free, an output pin of this core, or owned by id.

name: claim
text: Make id the owner of the pin ("pin taken" if the other core got it first).

name: (claim)
text: claim, keeping the pin.

name: release
text: Free every pin id owns.

name: cid
text: The owner id while spi-open claims its pins.

name: unit
text: The owner register of peripheral u (section 5.16, *Peripheral owners*).

name: (unit)
text: Take peripheral u for this core; "in use by the other core" if the other core has it.

name: unit-free
text: Let peripheral u go.

name: (i2c)
text: Give the I2C master a command and wait until it is done; "i2c timeout" when a slave held SCL low too long.

name: (i2c-free)
text: The bus recovery of i2c-open-pins: 9 clocks on SCL with SDA released, then a stop, with the pins as GPIO before the master takes them.

name: (i2c-line)
text: Release (true) or pull low (false) an I2C line as GPIO, then wait 10 µs.

name: (i2c-wait)
text: Wait 10 µs.

name: (i2c-scl)
text: The pins i2c-open-pins was given.

name: (i2c-sda)
text: The pins i2c-open-pins was given.

name: (ack?)
text: "no ack" (after a stop) if f is false.

name: dds-sync
text: Wait until the DDS took over the last change (it runs on its own clock).

name: core#
text: The number of this core: 0 or 1 (0 on the single-core firmware).
examples: : hello ." core " core# . ." here" cr ;

name: send
text: Send x to the other core; waits while its mailbox is full.
examples: : worker begin receive dup * send again ;   \ core 1
: ask ( n -- n*n ) send receive ;   \ core 0

name: receive
text: The oldest cell the other core sent; waits until there is one.
examples: : worker begin receive dup * send again ;   \ core 1
: ask ( n -- n*n ) send receive ;   \ core 0

name: mail?
text: True if a cell is waiting for this core.

name: lock
text: Take lock n (0..7), waiting while the other core holds it. "bad lock" for other numbers.
examples: : bump 1000 0 do 0 lock shared @ 1+ shared ! 0 unlock loop ;   \ on both cores

name: try-lock
text: Take lock n if it is free or already this core's: true; false if the other core holds it.

name: unlock
text: Release lock n, if this core holds it.
examples: : bump 1000 0 do 0 lock shared @ 1+ shared ! 0 unlock loop ;   \ on both cores

name: shared
text: Address of the shared memory ($101000).
examples: : bump 1000 0 do 0 lock shared @ 1+ shared ! 0 unlock loop ;   \ on both cores
0 shared !   \ core 0, before
shared @ .   \ after both: 2000

name: /shared
text: Its size in bytes: 4096.

name: (lock)
text: The register of lock n: reads 0 free, 1 this core's, 2 the other's.

name: owner
text: Pin owners. owner ( pin -- id ) shows who owns a pin: 0 nobody (the pin is GPIO), 1..4 PWM channels 0..3, 5 UART 0, 6 UART 1, 7 SPI 0, 8 SPI 1, 9 I2C, 10 the DDS, 15 an output pin;

name: pin-miso
text: The SPI header's pins are pin-sck, pin-mosi, pin-miso and pin-ss.
examples: pin-sck pin-mosi pin-miso 0 spi-open  1000000 0 spi-hz

name: pin-mosi
text: The SPI header's pins are pin-sck, pin-mosi, pin-miso and pin-ss.
examples: pin-sck pin-mosi pin-miso 0 spi-open  1000000 0 spi-hz

name: pin-sck
text: The SPI header's pins are pin-sck, pin-mosi, pin-miso and pin-ss.
examples: pin-sck pin-mosi pin-miso 0 spi-open  1000000 0 spi-hz

name: pin-scl
text: The shield's SCL and SDA pins (pin-scl, pin-sda) have pull-up resistors on the board and are the default;

name: pin-sda
text: The shield's SCL and SDA pins (pin-scl, pin-sda) have pull-up resistors on the board and are the default;

name: pin-ss
text: The SPI header's pins are pin-sck, pin-mosi, pin-miso and pin-ss.
examples: pin-ss output pin-ss high   \ the chip select, idle high
pin-ss low $9F 0 spi-xfer drop 0 0 spi-xfer . pin-ss high   \ e.g. a flash's ID
